items.title: CM Revanth accuses KCR’s family of holding land above legally allowed limit
items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Wednesday, September 16, alleged in the Assembly that BRS chief K Chandrashekar Rao and his family members own land far in excess of the limits prescribed under the Telangana Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act. He said an inquiry will be conducted into alleged encroachment of government land by KCR and his family. CM Revanth said the law permits a maximum holding of 27 acres, and alleged that former CM KCR and his wife own 67.13 acres in Siddipet district. “We have seen people agitating for a cause, losing everything they owned. But one family benefitted immensely in Telangana in the name of statehood agitation and its aftermath,” CM Revanth said. He alleged that KCR’s farmhouse in Erravelli was spread over more than 700 acres, including 388 acres of government land meant to be assigned to Dalit families for livelihood. He said the government would inquire into the land and planned to distribute the land among 800 Dalit families. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: Survivor identified, cops probe more alleged victims and locations
items.summary: The Chennai police have identified the minor girl allegedly sexually assaulted by Gem Granites and Gem group of companies founder R Veeramani. Chennai police received a video of the assault in October 2025, but arrested Veeramani only ten months later in August 2026. The survivor’s statement has now been recorded before a Judicial Magistrate, marking a major breakthrough in the POCSO case that the Chennai police had earlier attempted to close. The police had earlier tried to drop the investigation claiming that the survivor’s identity could not be confirmed. However, a Special Court judge for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) refused to accept the police’s closure report, forcing the Chennai police to reopen the case, leading to Veeramani’s arrest. According to police sources, the survivor in her statement identified herself and Veeramani in the video. Since she belongs to a Scheduled Caste community, provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, have also been invoked in the case. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: Rs 14 cr in 9 days in just 1 state: The ever-expanding Modi celebration machine
items.summary: It’s birthday season for the prime minister again. PM Narendra Modi turns a year older today, and right on cue, his government, an assortment of BJP-run states, and the party itself are gearing up to stretch the celebrations into a full month of inaugurations, foundation-stone ceremonies and publicity blitzes. In Delhi, the state government and BJP plan to roll out the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan – Jan Seva Hi Prabhu Seva Hai” programme, running from September 17 all the way to October 18, with this year’s milestone also conveniently lining up with roughly 25 years since Modi first became Gujarat’s chief minister. Meanwhile, the Haryana government has allocated Rs 10 lakh to every Deputy Commissioner in the state for the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. Gujarat, as it turns out, has its own precedent. For a nine-day “ Vikas Saptah ” event last October marking 24 years since Modi first took charge as CM, the state government spent Rs 14.05 crore, according to an assembly reply to Congress MLA Jignesh Mevani.
